reference: User's 225787.jpg: fine outlined painted medieval atlas, muted greens and ochres.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: seamless transparent repeating artwork tile for a Halloween map-switch transition in Crownlands, a medieval hand-painted atlas strategy game.
Primary request: a restrained windblown flock of small ink-dark bats and a few ochre autumn leaves, on a genuinely transparent background. This is the Halloween replacement artwork for an existing pale-cloud transition, not a terrain map.
Art direction inspired by a painted medieval atlas: fine irregular dark ink outlines, soft matte watercolor shading, weathered natural textures; subdued charcoal, brown-black, muted aubergine wing highlights and faded ochre/russet leaves. No bright cartoon colors.
Composition: square 1024px tile. About 20 small bats distributed irregularly across the entire canvas, varied wings-open and wings-curled silhouettes, seen from slightly above like atlas drawings. Bat wingspans about 55-100px at 1024px canvas size. About 12 scattered dry curled oak/maple leaves, smaller than bats. Plenty of transparent space, around 75 percent of canvas empty. Bats remain individually recognizable with a tiny pointed-eared head and curved scalloped wings. Natural fine painted texture, not flat clipart.
No fog, clouds, opaque background, land, scenery, buildings, pumpkin faces, text, border, logos or watermark. Bats and leaves are independent cutouts with true alpha; no checkerboard baked into the image. Keep the tile boundaries quiet and transparent so repeating the tile does not expose hard seams. Grounded medieval Halloween mood, charming and mildly eerie.
